title: plan-record.v1 — one plan's head pointer, revision ledger, and gate evidence
description: The small mutable file beside a plan's immutable revisions. The revisions are the plan; this record says which one is current, what the chain of them has been, and what gates the plan has passed. It is the ONLY mutable file in a plan folder, which is what makes the compare-and-swap on `current.revision` sufficient to serialize every writer. Lifecycle status is deliberately absent: status is DERIVED from the evidence below (an approval, a review, a seal, a build binding) every time it is asked for, never stored, so a stored phase can never disagree with the evidence it claims to summarize.

slug.description: The folder name: a readable stem plus a short id suffix. Minted once and never changed — a retitle updates `title` and leaves the folder alone, because moving a folder to track a title breaks every path an operator or a script already holds.

snapshot.description: The revision file, relative to the plan folder. Pattern-constrained because this string is JOINED ONTO A FILESYSTEM PATH: an absolute value or one carrying `..` would let an imported record choose where the store writes. The shape matches what the store itself mints and nothing else.

current.description: The head. `revision` doubles as the compare-and-swap token every mutating verb must present.

ledger.description: Every revision ever minted, oldest first and contiguous from 1. Append-only: a revision is never rewritten and never removed, because a reader who sees only the head cannot tell a settled decision from a reversed one. Redaction excises a BODY and leaves its entry standing.

closure.description: How this plan ended, when it has. Recorded rather than derived because none of the three endings leaves a trace anywhere else: a merged Build looks the same from here as an abandoned one.

Pattern-constrained because this string is JOINED ONTO A FILESYSTEM PATH: an absolute value or one carrying `..` would let an imported record choose where the store writes. The shape matches what the store itself mints and nothing else.

redacted.description: This revision's BODY was deliberately excised. The entry, its digest, and its place in the chain remain, so the record still shows that a revision existed here and what it hashed to — a redaction is visible, never a hole that reads like an accident.

approval.description: Bound to a DIGEST, not to the plan: revising the plan retires the approval by construction, because the thing approved no longer exists.

plan_review.description: ONE cold review per approved revision. Folding fixes in as later revisions does NOT re-run it: a plan whose every revision re-triggered a panel would never converge, which is the failure the Build side already removed.

seal.description: TERMINAL and single-minted. Records both the digest that was reviewed and the digest that was sealed, so the gap between them — the fixes folded in after the review — is disclosable rather than invisible. There is no sealed-but-failed state: a plan with blocking findings simply stays an unsealed draft carrying them.

closure.description: `complete` — the Build it authorized was merged. `retired` — superseded by a later plan, kept for the record. `abandoned` — deliberately dropped. All three keep the plan and its revisions on the shelf; none of them deletes anything.
